span.label: THE DISSOCIATION IS MADE OF CORRELATIONS, NOT OF MEANS, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN. One measure (the N400), one design, two kinds of priming, and the question is whether each effect's size tracks how well the individual participant could see the prime: `unlike repetition priming in Experiment 1, for semantic priming in Experiment 2, VISIBILITY OF PRIMES AT 40 MS ... PREDICTED THE N400 EFFECT`. Individual differences are the instrument - a median split on d-prime - so the NULL in Experiment 1 is the informative half, not the weak one. It is also the paper's defence against its own worst confound: if repetition priming ran on conscious leakage, the participants who leaked more would prime more, and they do not
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE AUTOMATIC/CONTROLLED LINE MOVES OFF THE REPRESENTATION AND ONTO THE MECHANISM: `IT IS NOT THE TYPE OF REPRESENTATION (form or meaning) that determines the automaticity of priming effects, BUT RATHER THE TYPE OF MECHANISM utilized (pre-activation versus establishing connections).` The older account - form is automatic, meaning is not - would have to say the repetition effect is mostly form, and the authors call that assumption AD HOC in their own words rather than defending it. What replaces it is a distinction between raising the activation of a shared representation and building a link between two different ones, and only the second needs attention
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THEY NAME THE RESULT THAT WOULD REFUTE THEM, which almost nothing else in this corpus does: `finding evidence of N400 priming effects on masked TARGETS would strengthen the case for the N400 being a direct reflection of automatic processing and WOULD FORCE THOSE OF US WHO HAVE ASSUMED that it reflects a post-lexical stage of comprehension TO RETHINK OUR POSITION.` A named observation, a design that would produce it (mask the target instead of the prime), and the authors' own position placed at risk by it. The corpus holds many predictions; this is a stated disconfirmer
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A SECOND, SHARPER TEST IS SPECIFIED WITH ITS DISCRIMINATING PREDICTION: translation equivalents in bilinguals (arbre-TREE). `Quotation withheld.` That separates the two accounts cleanly - a translation equivalent is semantically related but shares no form, so the form-versus-meaning account predicts it behaves like semantic priming while the pre-activation account predicts it behaves like repetition priming. The prediction is stated in the direction that would embarrass the authors' preferred story if it failed
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THIS IS THE STUDY THAT CONTROLLED WHAT Kiefer DID NOT, AND Kiefer2012 IS IN THIS CORPUS - tagged tonight, four records earlier. `Quotation withheld.` The go/no-go animal-probe task exists to hold attention on the prime epoch constant across durations, because otherwise a shorter prime is also a less-attended one and the two are confounded. So the corpus now holds Kiefer's gating account, this paper's methodological objection to the evidence for it, and both papers' own hedges

span.label: repetition priming —contrasted-with→ semantic priming
span.note: differs in: WHETHER THE EFFECT TRACKS HOW WELL THE PRIME WAS SEEN. Semantic priming correlates with prime visibility across participants; repetition priming does not. Same measure, same design, so the difference is in the priming and not in the instrument - and on the authors' account it is a difference of MECHANISM (pre-activation versus establishing connections) rather than of representation · strength of the relation: 0.9 — THE PAPER'S CENTRAL RESULT. Grounded on the sentence that states BOTH arms so a reader cannot take half of it, and the conditional `If we further hypothesize` is left in because the correlation is the finding while the resource account is the interpretation.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: prime visibility —causes→ semantic priming
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.8 — WEIGHTED 0.8 AND `causes` IS DOING MORE WORK THAN THE DATA DO. This is a CORRELATION ACROSS PARTICIPANTS - nothing was manipulated between the people who saw more and the people who saw less - and the paper's own words are `likely played a role`, which is in the quote. The vocabulary has no `covaries-with`, so the note carries what the type cannot. No effect_direction: see the comment above this edge.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: pre-activation —causes→ repetition priming
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.8 — THE PROPOSED MECHANISM, AND THE HEDGES ARE THE FIRST WORDS OF THE QUOTE: `One way to avoid this relatively ad-hoc assumption WOULD BE TO ARGUE`. This is the authors' preferred account offered as an alternative to one they have just called ad hoc, not a result. Weight 0.8 for that reason - it is the lowest-evidenced row on this record and the most interesting one.

span.label: Robust N400 repetition priming appeared even for primes displayed too briefly to be identified.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: For repetition priming, individual prime visibility was unrelated to the size of the N400 effect at the shortest prime duration, arguing against conscious leakage as its source.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: For semantic priming, by contrast, prime visibility at 40 ms did predict the size of the N400 effect.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Direct between-experiment comparison showed repetition priming produced a larger N400 effect than semantic priming.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: No post-N400 late positivity effect of repetition was found, even for clearly visible primes, unlike earlier unmasked studies.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The authors conclude that previously reported masked semantic priming effects were plausibly driven by conscious leakage on a subset of trials rather than by unconscious processing.
